1800: of Hebrew origin (אֱנוֹשׁ); Enos (i.e. Enosh), a patriarch:--Enos.
1801: middle voice from a compound of ἐν and οὖς; to take in one's ear, i.e. to listen:--hearken.
1802: of Hebrew origin (חֲנוֹךְ); Enoch (i.e. Chanok), an antediluvian:--Enoch.
1804: from ἐκ and the base of ἄγγελος; to publish, i.e. celebrate:--shew forth.
1805: from ἐκ and ἀγοράζω; to buy up, i.e. ransom; figuratively, to rescue from loss (improve opportunity):--redeem.
1806: from ἐκ and ἄγω; to lead forth:--bring forth (out), fetch (lead) out.
1807: from ἐκ and αἱρέομαι; actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release:--deliver, pluck out, rescue.
1808: from ἐκ and αἴρω; to remove:--put (take) away.
1809: middle voice from ἐκ and αἰτέω; to demand (for trial):--desire.
1810: from ἐκ and the base of αἰφνίδιος; of a sudden (unexpectedly):--suddenly. Compare ἐξάπινα.
1811: from ἐκ and ἀκολουθέω; to follow out, i.e. (figuratively) to imitate, obey, yield to:--follow.
1812: plural ordinal from ἕξ and ἑκατόν; six hundred:--six hundred.
1813: from ἐκ and ἀλείφω; to smear out, i.e. obliterate (erase tears, figuratively, pardon sin):--blot out, wipe away.
1814: from ἐκ and ἅλλομαι; to spring forth :--leap up.
1815: from ἐξανίστημι; a rising from death:--resurrection.
1816: from ἐκ and ἀνατέλλω; to start up out of the ground, i.e. germinate:--spring up.
1817: from ἐκ and ἀνίστημι; objectively, to produce, i.e. (figuratively) beget; subjectively, to arise, i.e. (figuratively) object:--raise (rise) up.
1818: from ἐκ and ἀπατάω; to seduce wholly:--beguile, deceive.
1819: from ἐκ and a derivative of the same as αἰφνίδιος; of a sudden, i.e. unexpectedly:--suddenly. Compare ἐξαίφνης.
1820: middle voice from ἐκ and ἀπορέω; to be utterly at a loss, i.e. despond:--(in) despair.
1821: from ἐκ and ἀποστέλλω; to send away forth, i.e. (on a mission) to despatch, or (peremptorily) to dismiss:--send (away, forth, out).
1822: from ἐκ and a derivative of ἄρτιος; to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher):--accomplish, thoroughly furnish.
1823: from ἐκ and ἀστράπτω; to lighten forth, i.e. (figuratively) to be radiant (of very white garments):--glistening.
1824: from ἐκ and the genitive case singular feminine of αὐτός (ὥρα being understood); from that hour, i.e. instantly:--by and by, immediately, presently, straightway.
1825: from ἐκ and ἐγείρω; to rouse fully, i.e. (figuratively) to resuscitate (from death), release (from infliction):--raise up.
1826: from ἐκ and (to go); to issue, i.e. leave (a place), escape (to the shore):--depart, get (to land), go out.
1827: from ἐκ and ἐλέγχω; to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish:--convince.
1828: from ἐκ and ἑλκύω; to drag forth, i.e. (figuratively) to entice (to sin):--draw away.
1829: from a comparative of ἐκ and a presumed (to spue); vomit, i.e. food disgorged:--vomit.
1830: from ἐκ and ἐρευνάω; to explore (figuratively):--search diligently.
1831: from ἐκ and ἔρχομαι; to issue (literally or figuratively):--come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad.
1832: third person singular present indicative of a compound of ἐκ and εἰμί; so also neuter present participle of the same (with or without some form of εἰμί expressed); impersonally, it is right (through the figurative idea of being out in public):--be lawful, let, X may(-est).
1833: from ἐκ and (to examine); to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. ascertain or interrogate:--ask, enquire, search.
1834: from ἐκ and ἡγέομαι; to consider out (aloud), i.e. rehearse, unfold:--declare, tell.
1835: the tenth multiple of ἕξ; sixty:--sixty(-fold), threescore.
1836: from ἔχω (in the sense of taking hold of, i.e. adjoining); successive:--after, following, X morrow, next.
1837: middle voice from ἐκ and ἠχέω; to "echo" forth, i.e. resound (be generally reported):--sound forth.
1838: from ἔχω; habit, i.e. (by implication) practice:--use.
1839: from ἐκ and ἵστημι; to put (stand) out of wits, i.e. astound, or (reflexively) become astounded, insane:--amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder.
1840: from ἐκ and ἰσχύω; to have full strength, i.e. be entirely competent:--be able.
1841: from ἐκ and ὁδός; an exit, i.e. (figuratively) death:--decease, departing.
1842: from ἐκ and ὀλοθρεύω; to extirpate:--destroy.
1843: from ἐκ and ὁμολογέω; to acknowledge or (by implication, of assent) agree fully:--confess, profess, promise.
1844: from ἐκ and ὁρκίζω; to exact an oath, i.e. conjure:--adjure.
1845: from ἐξορκίζω; one that binds by an oath (or spell), i.e. (by implication) an "exorcist" (conjurer):--exorcist.
1846: from ἐκ and ὀρύσσω; to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing):--break up, pluck out.
1847: from ἐκ and a derivative of the neuter of οὐδείς; to make utterly nothing of, i.e. despise:--set at nought. See also ἐξουθενέω.
1848: a variation of ἐξουδενόω and meaning the same:--contemptible, despise, least esteemed, set at nought.
1849: from ἔξεστι (in the sense of ability); privilege, i.e. (subjectively) force, capacity, competency, freedom, or (objectively) mastery (concretely, magistrate, superhuman, potentate, token of control), delegated influence:--authority, jurisdiction, liberty, power, right, strength.
1850: from ἐξουσία; to control:--exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of.
1851: from a compound of ἐκ and ἔχω (meaning to stand out); prominence (figuratively):--principal.
1852: from ἔξυπνος; to waken:--awake out of sleep.
1853: from ἐκ and ὕπνος; awake:--X out of sleep.
1854: adverb from ἐκ; out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively:--away, forth, (with-)out (of, -ward), strange.
1856: from ἐκ and (to push); to expel; by implication, to propel:--drive out, thrust in.
1858: from ἑορτή; to observe a festival:--keep the feast.
1859: of uncertain affinity; a festival:--feast, holyday.
1860: from ἐπαγγέλλω; an announcement (for information, assent or pledge; especially a divine assurance of good):--message, promise.
1861: from ἐπί and the base of ἄγγελος; to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself:--profess, (make) promise.
1862: from ἐπαγγέλλω; a self-committal (by assurance of conferring some good):--promise.
1863: from ἐπί and ἄγω; to superinduce, i.e. inflict (an evil), charge (a crime):--bring upon.
1864: from ἐπί and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle for:--earnestly contend for.
1865: from ἐπί and (to assemble); to accumulate:--gather thick together.
1866: from ἐπαινέω; praised; Epænetus, a Christian:--Epenetus.
1867: from ἐπί and αἰνέω; to applaud:--commend, laud, praise.
1868: from ἐπί and the base of αἰνέω; laudation; concretely, a commendable thing:--praise.
1869: from ἐπί and αἴρω; to raise up (literally or figuratively):--exalt self, poise (lift, take) up.
1870: from ἐπί and αἰσχύνομαι; to feel shame for something:--be ashamed.
1871: from ἐπί and αἰτέω; to ask for:--beg.
1872: from ἐπί and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany:--follow (after).
1873: from ἐπί and ἀκούω; to hearken (favorably) to:--hear.
1874: from ἐπί and the base of ἀκροατής; to listen (intently) to:--hear.
1875: from ἐπί and ἄν; a particle of indefinite contemporaneousness; whenever, as soon as:--when.
1876: neuter of a presumed compound of ἐπί and ἀνάγκη; (adverbially) on necessity, i.e. necessarily:--necessary.
1877: from ἐπί and ἀνάγω; to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return:--launch (thrust) out, return.
1878: from ἐπί and ἀναμιμνήσκω; to remind of:--put in mind.
1879: middle voice from ἐπί and ἀναπαύω; to settle on; literally (remain) or figuratively (rely):--rest in (upon).
1880: from ἐπί and ἀνέρχομαι; to come up on, i.e. return:--come again, return.
1881: middle voice from ἐπί and ἀνίστημι; to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack:--rise up against.
1882: from a compound of ἐπί and ἀνορθόω; a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation):-- correction.
1883: from ἐπί and ἄνω; up above, i.e. over or on (of place, amount, rank, etc.):--above, more than, (up-)on, over.
1884: from ἐπί and ἀρκέω; to avail for, i.e. help:--relieve.
1885: from a compound of ἐπί and ἄρχω (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch"); a special region of government, i.e. a Roman præfecture:--province.
1886: from ἐπί and an equivalent of αὐλή; a hut over the head, i.e. a dwelling:--habitation.
1887: from ἐπί and αὔριον; occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (ἡμέρα being implied) to-morrow:--day following, morrow, next day (after).
1888: from ἐπί and αὐτός and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of (a thief); in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime:--in the very act.
1889: contracted from Ἐπαφρόδιτος; Epaphras, a Christian:--Epaphras.
1890: from ἐπί and ἀφρίζω; to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion):--foam out.
1891: from ἐπί (in the sense of devoted to) and (Venus); Epaphroditus, a Christian:--Epaphroditus. Compare Ἐπαφρᾶς.
1892: from ἐπί and ἐγείρω; to rouse upon, i.e. (figuratively) to excite against:--raise, stir up.
1893: from ἐπί and εἰ; thereupon, i.e. since (of time or cause):--because, else, for that (then, -asmuch as), otherwise, seeing that, since, when.
1894: from ἐπεί and δή; since now, i.e. (of time) when, or (of cause) whereas:--after that, because, for (that, -asmuch as), seeing, since.
1895: from ἐπειδή and περ; since indeed (of cause):--forasmuch.
1896: and other moods and persons of the same tense; from ἐπί and εἴδω; to regard (favorably or otherwise):--behold, look upon.
1897: from ἐπεί and περ; since indeed (of cause):--seeing.
1898: from a compound of ἐπί and εἰσάγω; a superintroduction:--bringing in.
1899: from ἐπί and εἶτα; thereafter:--after that(-ward), then.
